A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSM-based neural operator and universality result, with ST-SSM renamed SS-NO. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE benchmark evaluations and experiments on directionality, temporal memory, teacher forcing, factorization, and normalization.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, including added Euler experiments and damping/frequency ablations, alongside retained experimental analyses.

M1.justification: The bidirectional spatial S4D processing, sequential spatial factorization, temporal memory module, training objective, and model pseudocode remain substantively unchanged. Learned damping and frequency modulation already appear in v1 Sections 4–4.2; their stronger emphasis and new ablations do not establish new method components.

E1.justification: v2 adds compressible Euler Richtmeyer–Meshkov and gravitational Rayleigh–Taylor benchmarks, extending evaluation to compressible interface instabilities and gravitationally forced flows. Burgers, KS, the three Navier–Stokes datasets, and missing-context scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds temporal S4 modules to U-Net and Factformer and replaces multi-input FNO2D with an S4-augmented comparator. Separate Markovian and multi-input FFNO rows disappear; S4-augmented FFNO remains under the FFNO name, with its documented activation changed from GELU to ReLU. GKT remains multi-input despite its shorter name.

E3.justification: Appendix E changes augmentation from randomly sampled noise standard deviations to fixed dataset-specific values and changes GKT's reported budget from 50 to 500 epochs. Its downsampling description changes from time to space. New experiments specify 16/32/64-state ablations and Euler training/prediction protocols. v2's main-text noise variance conflicts with its appendix settings.

E4.justification: v2 Section 6.3 adds controlled damping/frequency ablations across three capacities and viscosities, plus analyses of learned damping distributions. The missing-context comparison is revised, while v1's normalization study and Table 6 are removed. Directionality, memory-window, teacher-forcing, and factorization studies are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly identifies main results as means over five independently seeded runs and gives standard-deviation bounds with exceptions. Its damping analyses aggregate five trained models and report significance p-values. v1 provides no corresponding run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice; an increase from a known earlier run count is not established.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark scores are replaced under revised settings, and Euler and damping results are added. SS-NO's TorusVis/TorusVisForce entries change from 0.0287/0.0286 to 0.0218/0.0263. The KS resolution-128, viscosity-0.1 entry changes from 0.0027 to 0.0026 in Table 1, although v2 Table 4 retains 0.0027. Missing-context rankings also change, and normalization results disappear.

T1.justification: The full-field-of-view assumptions, universality theorem, and complete proof remain unchanged as Appendix A becomes Appendix B. The limited additions are explicit mathematical definitions of Euler initial fields, perturbed interfaces, and gravitational equilibrium profiles in v2 Appendices F.4–F.5.

C1.justification: v2 extends headline performance claims to compressible Euler flows and explicitly claims damping stabilizes learning. The central claims of universality, F-FNO recovery, adaptive kernels, and parameter-efficient spatiotemporal operator learning already appear in v1.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantial explanations linking damping to capacity constraints and chaotic dynamics. Appendix C.2 acknowledges FFNO outperforming SS-NO without context and proposes residual connections as a possible explanation. The conclusion and new Appendix H add substantive limitations concerning irregular domains and memory costs of autoregressive backpropagation.

D1.justification: v2 documents Euler initial conditions, field selection, downsampling, splits, and prediction horizons, including availability of tracer and gravitational inputs at every timestep. It also newly specifies damping initialization and best-validation-loss selection. These materially expand reproducibility information, while the earlier normalization-specific documentation is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Herde et al.'s Poseidon dataset reference and Nair–Hinton's ReLU reference, while removing the Hendrycks–Gimpel GELU reference. It describes MemNO as a general operator framework rather than an FNO-specific backbone. The principal positioning relative to FNO, factorization, and spatial SSM work remains.

P1.justification: The title and model terminology change, and the introduction, method exposition, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Existing objective and metric sections move from Appendix E into the main text. The narrative is reorganized around damping and frequency learning, with revised appendix organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds three damping-distribution figures and an ablation table, moves both architecture diagrams into the main text, and merges/redraws the contextual-information plots. Benchmark tables change structure and the 2D table gains Euler columns; the normalization table disappears. Typography, margins, and figure sizing also change throughout.

improvement.justification: The controlled component ablations, more uniformly memory-augmented baselines, and five-seed reporting strengthen empirical substantiation. Added Euler tests and explicit failure conditions improve understanding of applicability. These gains are tempered by removal of the normalization comparison and reporting inconsistencies, including conflicting noise specifications and the differing KS entries in v2 Tables 1 and 4.
